parameters.text:
=You are parsing a cosmetic product formula PDF from PT Astoria Prima. The raw extracted text is below between <document> tags. Extract exactly what is printed - never invent, guess or calculate a value that is not present.

Return ONLY a JSON object with this exact shape:
{
  "ffs": "formula code, e.g. MR03-BN-01",
  "kategori": "product category as printed",
  "customer": "customer name as printed",
  "bj": number or null,
  "phMin": number or null,
  "phMax": number or null,
  "viscosity": "range as printed, e.g. '20000 - 30000 cP'",
  "stabTk": "Running | Pass | Fail | -",
  "stabTkul": "Running | Pass | Fail | -",
  "stabT50": "Running | Pass | Fail | -",
  "stabTm": "Running | Pass | Fail | -",
  "note": "any general note",
  "multiTable": true | false,
  "lines": [ { "materialName": "as printed", "materialCode": "code if printed, else empty", "pct": number, "note": "" } ]
}

Rules:
- Values not present in the document must be null (numbers) or "" (strings) - never guessed.
- Percentages must sum to 100 across lines; copy them exactly as printed.
- If the document contains more than one formula table, extract only the primary (first/main) table and set "multiTable": true; otherwise set "multiTable": false.
- Output raw JSON only, no markdown fences, no commentary.

<document>
{{ $json.text }}
</document>
